title: Proton pump inhibitor use and dementia risk: prospective population-based study
authors: Gray SL, Walker RL, Dublin S, Yu O, Aiello Bowles EJ, Anderson ML, et al.
journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
population: Kaiser Permanente Washington members aged 65 years or older without dementia, screened every 2 years with standardised diagnostic evaluation (Adult Changes in Thought study)
funder: This work was supported by National Institute on Aging U01AG00678 (Dr. Larson). The sponsors did not play a role in design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; or in preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; or the decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
authorConflicts: EBL receives royalties from UpToDate; RLW received funding as a biostatistician from a Pfizer grant to Group Health Research Institute; OY from Bayer grants to the institute.
result: 827 participants (23.7%) developed dementia. PPI exposure was not associated with dementia (P = .66) or Alzheimer's disease (P = .77): HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.18) for 365, 0.99 (0.75 to 1.30) for 1095 and 1.13 (0.82 to 1.56) for 1825 total standardised daily doses, about 1, 3 and 5 years of daily use.
